summary: The candidate accurately captures nearly the entire framed-link-to-Reshetikhin–Turaev construction, including the principal theorems, convention-sensitive ribbon Hopf formulas, modular data, purification, and the selected normalization. Its main weaknesses are systematic entry-class errors, omission of a few standalone foundational or intermediate entries, a malformed or ambiguous categorical-trace formula, absent explicit external-attribution metadata, and avoidable duplication among auxiliary entries.
strengths: Correctly extracts the Lickorish–Wallace, Kirby calculus, Turaev ribbon-graph, purification, and Reshetikhin–Turaev theorems with accurate page locators.

Preserves the gold revision's Turaev-style conventions: the universal twist acts as theta_V=rho_V(v), the quantum trace uses rho_V(uv), and the displayed tau normalization agrees with the selected convention.
Covers the principal categorical infrastructure: strict monoidal structure, braiding, duality, ribbon category, graphical calculus, categorical trace and dimension, and colored ribbon graphs.
Covers the modular stage well, including the modular-category conditions, Hopf-link matrix, Kirby color, weighted surgery sum, rank D, Delta, modular Hopf algebra, and purification.
Includes several valid source-grounded supporting entries beyond the gold set, such as blackboard framing, pivotal data, colored Jones material, and the root-of-unity route to WRT invariants.
Entry identifiers and page numbers are generally descriptive and consistent with the source locations.
issues: Several entries are assigned unsuitable classes: the surgery construction, tensor-product action, and purification are labeled algorithm, while graphical-calculus rules, the trace relation, and the tau definition are labeled calculation rather than definition, fact, claim, or theorem-like infrastructure.

The categorical-trace formula is not properly grouped: the tensor product with id_{V*} appears outside the intended parenthesized composite, making the displayed expression mathematically ambiguous or ill-typed as written.
There is no standalone definition of a Hopf algebra, although this is foundational in the gold reference.

The R-matrix-induced braiding and antipode-induced rigid structure are only summarized inside broader entries; the explicit braiding formula and the full structural claims represented separately in the gold are not extracted.
Negligible modules are defined, but negligible morphisms and their trace-pairing condition are not explicitly defined even though purification depends on their ideal.

Handle-slide invariance and blow-up invariance are compressed into the final RT theorem instead of being represented as distinct intermediate results, reducing visibility of the two key Kirby-invariance mechanisms.

Named results from prior literature have null attribution metadata; names such as Lickorish–Wallace and Turaev communicate attribution informally but do not satisfy structured external-attribution handling.

The artifact contains redundant fragmentation: Yang–Baxter appears as both a proposition and a calculation, one hexagon identity repeats part of the braiding definition, and several colored-Jones entries substantially overlap.
Some extra proposition entries are too weak or tautological to merit independent entry status, notably the assertion that F(K;V_n) for n>1 is a higher colored Jones polynomial.

entryLevelComparison.note: The intrinsic framing definition is accurate, with an additional useful blackboard-framing entry.
The construction and notation are accurate, but this is a definition or fact rather than an algorithm.
The equivalence and all move types are faithfully stated.
The artifact begins using Hopf-algebra structure without extracting its standalone definition.
The central representation-category result and the twist convention are correct, though the induced braiding formula is not displayed.
The quantum-trace convention agrees with the gold reference.
The module definition is correct, but the accompanying definition of negligible morphisms is absent.
Kirby-move invariance is asserted globally, but handle-slide invariance is not extracted as its own structural result.
The selected normalization formula is correct but should be typed as a definition or fact, not a calculation.
The main result is accurately and comprehensively stated, including orientation-preserving homeomorphism invariance.
